reflection: Explain one choice to a partner.
title: Transparent & Opaque
description: Sort clear materials and opaque objects in a colourful light notebook.
brief: Look at the named material: can you see clearly through it?

groups.label: Transparent
groups.description: Light passes through; a clear view

items.label: Clear window
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="20" y="14" width="60" height="72" rx="3" fill="#b8deeb"/><path d="M50 14v72M20 50h60"/><path d="M28 38l12-14M58 77l14-16" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="5"/></svg>

items.label: Empty clear cup
items.art: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" fill="none" stroke="#254554" stroke-width="3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M27 22h46l-6 64H33z" fill="#cbe9ef" fill-opacity=".65"/><path d="M30 22c0-7 40-7 40 0M35 32l3 40" stroke="#729aa8"/></svg>

notes:
Focus: compare how light passes through materials. These cards are deliberately transparent or opaque. Translucent materials, such as frosted glass, let some light through but do not give a clear view.

Ask students to test real materials with a torch. Never look at the Sun through a lens.

Symbols are editable inline SVG; no generated image assets.
